clauses.reason: whole: EO 12095 (signed 1978-11-02, 43 FR 51595) creates an emergency board under section 44 of the Airline Deregulation Act of 1978 to investigate the dispute between Wien Air Alaska, Inc. and certain individuals represented by the Air Line Pilots Association. Its commands are the establishment of the board ("1-101. Establishment o f  Board.") and the thirty-day report command ("1-102. Report."); it contains no standstill. First end: EO 12379 (signed 1982-08-17, 47 FR 36099), whose preamble states that it is made "to terminate the establishing authorities for" committees that are inactive or no longer necessary and whose section 5 reads "Sec. 5. Executive Order No. 12095, creating an Em ergency Board to Investigate" (the sentence continues on the next line and ends "is revoked."). EO 12379 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1982-08-17. The Office of the Federal Register catalog note reads "Revoked by: EO 12379, August 17, 1982". Later event, not an end: the board's report dated February 9, 1979 (held NMB copy); the order was functionally spent on 1979-02-09. The held source-ladder files named for EO 11022, EO 11256 and EO 11829 are copies of the same 47 FR 36099 pages of EO 12379; the dossier's chain events dated 1962, 1965 and 1975 that cite them for this order come from those misnamed files and are not events.

research_rationale:
EO 12095 (signed 1978-11-02; 43 FR 51595, Federal Register of November 6, 1978) recites a dispute between Wien Air Alaska, Inc. and certain individuals represented by the Air Line Pilots Association and recites that section 44 of the Airline Deregulation Act of 1978 (Public Law 95-504) directed that section 10 of the Railway Labor Act be invoked; under section 44 it orders 1-101 (Establishment of Board: a board of three members to be appointed by the President to investigate the dispute, no member to be interested in any organization of airline employees or any carrier) and 1-102 (Report: the board reports its findings to the President "within 30 days from the date o f this Order."). The order contains no standstill or maintaining-conditions command. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12095.txt, PDF page 11) and confirmed its number, date, page and subject. First and whole-order end: express revocation by EO 12379 section 5 (signed 1982-08-17, no effective-date wording, read as effective on signing), from the held Federal Register text of EO 12379. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the board's report is a spent fact recorded as a later event: the held National Mediation Board copy of the report of Emergency Board No. 95-504 appointed by EO 12095 (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_12095_Wien_Air_Alaska_Air_Line_Pilots_Association_emergency_board_established_November2_197_5963629762.txt; PDF file sha256 060e9e9dbce19691f22a58039c2cfb0de7637147a6626d6f631760b09d6e0cd7) is dated February 9, 1979, and the order was functionally spent on 1979-02-09. Bounded search: the dossier's three machine searches, chosen after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning (U.S. Code release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with GovInfo CFR bulk XML; Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts); the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; a full read of EO 12379 (held FR text); and a read of the report's front matter and letter of transmittal (PDF pages 1-3).
